notes.label: Build a new three-stage floor-supported boundary puzzle from the empty template: open a release-face approach, independently offset a roof-limited rigid column, then raise a separate exit gate.
notes.goal: Build a new three-stage floor-supported boundary puzzle from the empty template: open a release-face approach, independently offset a roof-limited rigid column, then raise a separate exit gate.
notes.change: Use a horizontal parking shutter, a two-cell vertical roof column and a separate two-cell vertical gate, with a bent approach to the column's east face. Derive new floor corridors and one parking bay rather than copying the HxH stairs or support-loss layout.
notes.reason: The shutter must expose the only approach to the release stance; the roof column must disengage before the gate can rise; the gate must then clear the only gem corridor. All three stages affect the next functional operation.
expectedChecks: No first release opportunity without parking the shutter
No gate-up opportunity without offsetting the roof column
Matched roof removal admits the blocked gate input and a goal bypass without column offset
Ordinary saved-build replay and browser play/save/export

notes.label: Improve recovery after the roof column has been released, while preserving the three connected functional stages.
notes.goal: Improve recovery after the roof column has been released, while preserving the three connected functional stages.
notes.change: Add a lower circulation aisle at (6,8), (7,8), and (8,8), so a gate moved downward once can be approached from below and restored.
notes.reason: The first layout passes its declared dependency checks, but inspection exposes an avoidable irreversible gate-down mistake after release. The recovery aisle may also allow a downward completion; rerun the existing directional claim and retain any counterexample before revising the claim.
expectedChecks: Three necessary rigid roles remain necessary
Shutter parking still precedes column release
Column release still precedes gate progress
Retest whether upward gate motion remains necessary
Ordinary replay of any gate-down bypass

notes.label: Keep the recovery aisle and state the dependency actually supported by the revised map.
notes.goal: Keep the recovery aisle and state the dependency actually supported by the revised map.
notes.change: Replace the upward-only final-stage event with movement of the exit gate in either legal direction. Keep the ordinary upward witness and exact spatial checks, and add a selected-state recovery check.
notes.reason: The fresh check found and ordinarily replayed a complete route without M1-up. It still requires parking M2, independently offsetting M0, and moving M1 afterward. The failed directional necessity result is retained; the final claim concerns gate movement, not a unique direction or solution order beyond the tested dependencies.
expectedChecks: Gate movement is necessary for the real gem objective
No gate movement opportunity before column-left
A single gate-down mistake can be restored from the new aisle
Replay the preserved downward bypass using ordinary engine moves
